title: HINT for Proposals — claims stay inside the offer
metaDescription: Keep customer requirements, approved claims, proof and commitments beside proposals so assistants do not promise what delivery cannot support.
h1: Your assistant writes proposals fast. HINT keeps every promise supportable.
intro: HINT keeps customer requirements, approved offer language, proof and approval boundaries in plain-text notes beside a pursuit. Your assistant reads the context for this opportunity before drafting an answer.

situations.before: A strong claim appears without a case study or approved proof.
situations.body: The assistant links the claim to support or marks it for review instead of polishing uncertainty into certainty.

situations.before: A helpful sentence becomes a contractual delivery commitment.
situations.body: Dates, service levels and custom work must come from the approved offer and named approver.

situations.before: A response says compliant but never points to the answer.
situations.body: Each customer requirement links to the proposal section and proof that addresses it.

example.intro: The Monorail proposal demo grounds a pursuit answer in an approved source.
example.after: It drafts inside the approved offer and lists unsupported references, prices or delivery promises for review.
example.compiled:
<answer name="springfield-monorail-1">
  Approved answer grounded in SRC-1.
</answer>
<never name="Invented details">…</never>

never: Invent a customer reference, price, proof point or commitment.
Claim compliance without mapping to an answer and evidence.
Turn an unresolved clarification into a convenient assumption.
disclaimer: HINT supports proposal drafting; commercial, legal and delivery owners remain responsible for approvals and contractual commitments.

faq.q: Does it write the whole proposal?
faq.a: It can help draft sections from declared pursuit context, but the package intentionally has no deterministic emit surface for answers that require judgment.
Yes. Shared proof and offer language can be included while opportunity-specific promises remain scoped to the pursuit.

faq.q: Can it decide that a requirement is compliant?
faq.a: No. It can show the declared answer and evidence; an authorized reviewer owns the compliance decision.

keywordDescriptions.pursuit: Sets the customer, opportunity and response boundary.
keywordDescriptions.requirement: Records a customer request with its source reference.
keywordDescriptions.answer: Drafts a response linked to the requirement it addresses.
keywordDescriptions.offer: Defines the approved commercial and delivery envelope.
keywordDescriptions.claim: States an assertion that needs approved support.
keywordDescriptions.proof: Identifies evidence supporting a proposal claim.
keywordDescriptions.pricing: Records sourced commercial terms and approval.
keywordDescriptions.commitment: Records a promise with owner and approval.
keywordDescriptions.legalreview: Marks language that requires authorized legal review.
